title: How many boxes does school cover on the strip?
description: A strip of forty eight boxes records one day in half hour boxes. The video turns the school hours into boxes and finds the box where school starts, and breaks Keeko's doubt that one hour is one box.
teaching_notes: One idea: two boxes make one hour, so hours are multiplied by two to get boxes. Watch for students who take one box for each hour.

source: {{NAME_5}}'s school runs from 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. How many boxes
video_script.why: A strip turns the clock into boxes, so the child must change hours into boxes and find a position on the strip.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the hours by two for the boxes, and count the boxes before the start to find the first box.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_5}}'s strip of forty eight boxes for one day
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says school is seven hours so it is seven boxes, taking one box for each hour.
video_script.payoff_line: multiply seven by two to get fourteen boxes

final_answer.spoken: fourteen boxes, starting at box twenty

names.{{NAME_5}}: records his day on a strip of 48 boxes

maths_rules: 24 hours x 2 boxes = 48 boxes; box 1 begins at midnight; one box = half an hour
9:30 am to 4:30 pm = 7 hours; 7 x 2 = 14 boxes
9:30 am is 9.5 hours after midnight; 9.5 x 2 = 19 boxes come before it, so box 20 is the first school box; school covers boxes 20 to 33
slip: one box is half an hour, not one hour
video_script.design: One idea: hours times two gives boxes, and the boxes before the start give the first box. The wrong idea is one box for each hour. The strip of forty eight boxes stays on screen all video.

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='strip'/>{{NAME_5}} records the whole day on a strip of forty eight boxes.
<bookmark mark='hour'/>Two boxes of the strip make one hour of his day.
<bookmark mark='school'/>His school runs from nine thirty in the morning to four thirty in the afternoon.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many boxes does the school cover, and which box does it start at?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko appears at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the strip with pairs of boxes bracketed as hours; box 1 labelled midnight; one box labelled half an hour

marks.day: twenty four pairs of boxes are bracketed along the strip, one pair for each hour
marks.half: one box is labelled half an hour

narration: <bookmark mark='day'/>A day has twenty four hours, and two boxes for each hour make forty eight boxes.
<bookmark mark='start'/>Box one begins at midnight, and each box is only half an hour long.
<bookmark mark='half'/>That is why one box and one hour are not the same thing.

beats.on_screen: Given: 48 boxes for 24 hours; 2 boxes = 1 hour; school from 9:30 am to 4:30 pm

marks.given: the strip facts and the school times are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two boxes make one hour, and school runs from nine thirty to four thirty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of boxes the school covers, and the box where it starts

marks.find1: the number of boxes is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find1'/>We have to find how many boxes the school covers.
<bookmark mark='find2'/>We also find the box where it starts.

marks.clock: a clock face shows nine thirty and then four thirty
marks.hrs: seven hours is written between them

narration: <bookmark mark='clock'/>Step one, find the hours. From nine thirty in the morning to four thirty in the afternoon.
<bookmark mark='hrs'/>That is seven hours.

marks.two: two boxes are drawn under each of the seven hours
marks.mul: the working seven times two is written

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, each hour is two boxes.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Seven hours need seven times two boxes.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 9:30 am is 9.5 hours after midnight; boxes before the start = 9.5 x 2

marks.mid: the strip is counted from midnight up to nine thirty
marks.mul: the working nine and a half times two is written

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step three, find where the school starts. Nine thirty is nine and a half hours after midnight.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>The boxes before the start are nine and a half times two.

marks.box: fourteen boxes are shaded on the strip
marks.st: the first shaded box is marked as box twenty

narration: <bookmark mark='box'/>Multiply seven by two to get fourteen boxes.
<bookmark mark='st'/>Nineteen boxes come before nine thirty, so the school starts at box twenty.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the strip
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: seven boxes shaded under the label school, struck out; seven hours each with two boxes

marks.doubt: seven boxes are shaded under the label school
marks.two: the label is struck out and every hour is shown with two boxes
marks.fix: the shading grows to cover all the boxes of the seven hours

beats.removed: the seven box shading is struck out
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the school is seven boxes, because it is seven hours.
<bookmark mark='two'/>But one box is only half an hour. Every hour needs two boxes.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Seven hours of school need more boxes than seven.
